answer: Because the anchor index resolves every citation against the lantern checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the jetty audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 158 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 158 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 2663 identities would post 2282 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
